en: *The Diamond Scalpel*, one fascicle (including the preface). Although this text is not among the common scriptures or treatises, I wish to model it after them by dividing it into three sections: from the beginning up to "a single thought-moment" constitutes the Section on the Preface; from "Once, in a quiet night" down to "meeting with my son" constitutes the Section on the Main Exposition; and what follows constitutes the Section on the Propagation.

The main body of the exposition is roughly divided into ten sections: first, the formal establishment of the fundamental tenet; second, from "Thereupon, the wild guest" downward, the reconciliation of alternative names; third, from "Therefore we know that worldly people" downward, the exclusion of the false and the revelation of the true; fourth, from "I desire to provide guidance" downward... [and so forth].

1. From "The method for descending and emerging" (*xià chūfǎ zhèngtǐ*)—the fifth section, concerning the guest’s statement, which clarifies the meaning established by the Benevolent One (*rén*). 2. From "Distinguishing the inclusion of dharmas" (*biàn fǎshè*)—the sixth section, concerning the son’s statement, which examines what the son perceives. 3. From "Furthermore, what the son has grasped" (*rán zǐ suǒ lǐng*)—the seventh section, clarifying the lineage of the Dharma Master. 4.

From the guest’s statement, "I have heard this repeatedly" (*lǚ wén*)—the eighth section, which leads from delusion toward awakening. 5. From the guest’s statement, "This is an error" (*sī shī*)—the ninth section, which judges the school to which the teaching belongs. 6. From "One should know that the One Vehicle... (*dāng zhī yīchéng*)—the tenth section, which summarizes and refines [the preceding points]. This was recorded at the beginning because it represents the Master’s own critical assessment (*liào*).

Classified by the Śramaṇa Zhìyuán of Gūshān.
